title: Diwali Fonts, Symbols & Kaomoji Generator | UltraTextGen
meta_description: Style a Diwali greeting live, copy diya and firework emoji, sparkly kaomoji, curated ASCII art, and ready-made phrases with native script, romanization, and translation.
hero_tagline: Type a name or wish and style it in curated festive fonts, then copy diyas, fireworks, sparklers, and kaomoji — or tap a ready-made greeting to style it instantly.
intro: Diwali (Deepavali), the Festival of Lights, is one of the biggest gifting-and-greeting occasions of the year — rows of diyas on doorsteps, fireworks overhead, rangoli patterns underfoot, and messages wishing family and friends light, prosperity, and joy for the year ahead. This page gathers everything for styling that greeting: curated fonts you can preview on your own text, the diya-and-firework emoji people actually paste, sparkly kaomoji for a celebratory chat message, a handful of original ASCII art pieces, and a phrase bank of real greetings — native script, romanization, and translation — that restyle instantly when you tap them.
date_window: on a different date each year, in October or November, set by the Hindu lunar calendar

occurrence._source: Diwali main day (Lakshmi Puja, the Amavasya of Kartika). Cross-checked 2026-09-01 across diwali.info/diwali-dates, bda.ai and a web search summary; 2026-11-08 independently corroborates the figure in the 2026-07-31 events audit. NOT native-verified against a panchang — see _caution.
occurrence._caution: Do not source these from a page titled 'Lakshmi Puja' without checking which one it means. publicholidays.in gives 2026-10-25, because it documents Bengali Kojagari Lakshmi Puja (full moon of Ashwin, observed in Odisha/Tripura/West Bengal) — a different festival that shares the name. That mismatch is why this table carries a date_note rather than a bare date.

date_note: Regional traditions can observe Diwali a day either side of this, depending on when the tithi falls at dawn locally.
